builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Migrating a Legacy Scientific Application with an AI Coding Agent: NICAM from Fortran to Kokkos
summary: The technique replaces manual Fortran-to-C++/Kokkos porting of a large legacy scientific application with direct translation by an AI coding agent (Claude Code) under human review, converting roughly 140,000 lines of Fortran into 35,000 lines of C++/Kokkos. Costs include sustained human expert review, ensemble-based statistical validation (a 100-member comparison against the original model), and porting effort across the dynamical core and seven physics packages. What can fail: subtle numerical or behavioral divergence from the original model that statistical ensemble checks may miss, and performance portability is not guaranteed—the HIP build on MI300A only reached parity after bandwidth normalization, so gains depend on target hardware and kernel characteristics.
rationale: The reader has no legacy HPC codebase to migrate and no GH200/MI300A-class hardware, so this is a relevant proof point for agent-assisted code migration but not directly adoptable in their production practice.
technique: Agent-assisted legacy code migration to Kokkos

claims.statement: The technique replaces manual Fortran-to-C++/Kokkos porting of a large legacy scientific application with direct translation by an AI coding agent (Claude Code) under human review, converting roughly 140,000 lines of Fortran into 35,000 lines of C++/Kokkos. Costs include sustained human expert review, ensemble-based statistical validation (a 100-member comparison against the original model), and porting effort across the dynamical core and seven physics packages. What can fail: subtle numerical or behavioral divergence from the original model that statistical ensemble checks may miss, and performance portability is not guaranteed—the HIP build on MI300A only reached parity after bandwidth normalization, so gains depend on target hardware and kernel characteristics.

Application speedups of 1.71x on NVIDIA GH200 and 1.54x on AMD MI300A versus the Fortran/OpenACC baseline; CUDA kernel-time speedup of 1.38x on GH200; HIP on MI300A at 0.96x of baseline kernel performance after bandwidth normalization.
